Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. The focus marker =na attaches to O and patient-S NPs (absolutive position) while =en marks A (agent/instrument), creating a partial ergative/absolutive alignment. Frampton (2020:37): "the agent/instrument case-marking enclitic /=en/ is used to mark focus for agent subjects, while /=na/ performs the same function for object and patient subject, lending support to arguments for the existence of a partial ergative system." Source: Frampton 2020:12,37.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. 1sg pronoun a= takes =en in agent function: ex.5.77 "a=en yabi a=en pepa a-yam-i" (1sg.pro=agt father 1sg.pro=agt paper write-3pl.o); ex.5.78 "a=en mataa=ka a-faf-si-n" (1sg.pro=agt first carry). Source: Frampton 2020:59-60.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. 2sg pronoun e= takes =en in agent function: ex.5.73 "e=en yei ko-uki ku-wawe=ate" (2sg.pro=agt older.sibling go.down get). Source: Frampton 2020:59.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. 3rd person pronouns take =en as agent marker: ex.4.94 "ei=en aifi ti-nane" (3pl.pro=agt care they-do); ex.4.88 "Joanna=en au... 2.s-give" (proper name/agent). Source: Frampton 2020:42,59.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Full NPs take =en in agent function: ex.5.49 "ari sauki=en begati=e ti-ra" (3sg.gen wife=agt garden go); ex.5.72 "siko=en i-vasus-i" (pig=agt give.birth); ex.5.53 "damun nen=en" (torch=agt). Source: Frampton 2020:56,59.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. =en is not restricted by aspect. The grammar provides no aspect-based conditioning; =en marks agent subjects and instruments across contexts. Source: Frampton 2020:12,59-60.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. =en appears in past/perfective contexts: ex.5.55 "sauki=en begati=e ti-ra" in narrative past. Source: Frampton 2020:59-60.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. =en appears in past tense contexts throughout the corpus examples. Source: Frampton 2020:12,59-60.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. =en appears in non-past (future, habitual) contexts; no tense restriction stated. The marker is pragmatically conditioned (agent focus), not tense-conditioned. Source: Frampton 2020:12,59-60.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. All attested =en examples are in indicative declarative clauses. Source: Frampton 2020:12,59-60.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. =en appears in non-indicative (imperative) contexts: ex.5.73 "e=en yei ko-uki ku-wawe=ate" (2sg.pro=agt older.sibling go.down get) is an imperative/command. Source: Frampton 2020:59.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Ergative alignment occurs in realis contexts; all main examples are realis declaratives. Source: Frampton 2020:12,59-60.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. No irrealis restriction on =en stated in the grammar. The marker is pragmatically motivated (agent focus), not restricted to realis contexts. Source: Frampton 2020:12,59-60.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Agentive A is the prototypical context for =en: marks the "agent subject" of transitive verbs (Frampton 2020:59). Source: Frampton 2020:59.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Non-agentive A (instrument, natural force/cause) takes =en: ex.5.74-5.75 show instruments (skirt, knife) with =en; ex.5.76 "forogi=en i-kefot-si" (cloud=agt covered-it) shows a natural force. Frampton (2020:59): "It also marks nouns denoting a natural force such as wind, rain, clouds, etc. when they are functioning as subjects." Source: Frampton 2020:59.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: The morpheme =na marks a topicalised S/P; the morpheme =en marks the agent of a topicalised A or the agent in general
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Topical A takes =en; the topic+agent marker combination is attested (ex.4.94: "ei=en...ti-nane" where ei is a topicalized 3pl pronoun acting as agent). Source: Frampton 2020:12,37,59-60.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: The morpheme =na marks a topicalised S/P; the morpheme =en marks the agent of a topicalised A or the agent in general
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Non-topical A also takes =en. =en marks agent focus regardless of topicality; ex.5.76 "forogi=en" (cloud=agt) is non-topicalized. Source: Frampton 2020:12,37,59-60.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Animate A is the primary context for =en (human agents, animals: ex.5.72 pig=agt, ex.5.49 wife=agt). Source: Frampton 2020:59.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. Inanimate A (natural forces) also takes =en: ex.5.76 "forogi=en i-kefot-si" (cloud=agt covered-it). Frampton (2020:59): "It also marks nouns denoting a natural force such as wind, rain, clouds, etc." Source: Frampton 2020:59.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. All primary =en examples are in main clauses. Source: Frampton 2020:12,59-60.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. =en appears in non-main (medial/subordinate) clauses: ex.2.27 "siko=en i-vasus-i=na" (pig=agt give.birth-3pl.o=ds.sim) uses different-subject simultaneous medial suffix =na; ex.5.53 "damun nen=en" in a serial construction. Source: Frampton 2020:14,56.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 0. =en marks agent subjects without morphosyntactic conditioning by tense, aspect, mood, animacy, or person. Its optionality is pragmatic (focus marking for agents), not a morphosyntactic split. Frampton (2020:59): "The use of /=en/ to mark agent subject is not obligatory." Source: Frampton 2020:59.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
curated_comment: Confirmed value 0. Ergative/agent marker =en (Table 5, p.35: "Agent/Instrument") is formally distinct from all other case markers and possessive forms. No genitive case enclitic shares the form =en. Source: Frampton 2020:35,59.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Only valid for the =en morpheme, the marker of A.
curated_comment: Confirmed value 1. =en marks both agent AND instrument: Frampton (2020:59) section 5.3.5: "It also marks the instrument used for an action" (ex.5.74 skirt=agt, ex.5.75 knife=agt). Ergative and instrumental are expressed by the same marker. Source: Frampton 2020:59-60.
